items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: And then when we got to Richard Jones, piano player, come there... He had quite a name.

ctx.x: You see? And we're taking a job for a fella called Vincent Lepresto, a Paul Barnes band. Well we played for Vincent Lepresto through 33, and we were getting three dollars a night a man, and we would play two nights a week so that we made six dollars, and strange as it sounds, that six dollars was plenty of money at that time in 33, because some people wasn't, if they could make a dollar, I'm telling you, they would do good. They had people around there and some in the bread lines, and six dollars was, I used to…
Was that the songwriter, Hermione Jones from Chicago? I mean he came from here, but he wrote things like Trouble in Mind, do you remember? Was that the same one?
What's that said his name was? Richard Jones. Yeah, Richard Jones. Yeah, that's the same Richard Jones. He had quite a name.
